newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NedCar production to reach peak of 280,000 in '97.
newsitem.headline: NedCar production to reach peak of 280,000 in '97.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo on Friday said production at the NedCar plant in Born, Holland would reach its maximum annual capacity of 280,000 cars in September 1997.
"We plan to reach 280,000 cars per year in September 1997. Talks with Mitsubishi are not finalised, but this can be seen as a formality," Volvo Car spokesman Ingmar Hesslefors told Reuters.
The NedCar plant is a joint venture between Volvo, Mitsubishi Motors Corp and the Dutch state.
The plant produces Volvo's S40/V40 model and, until November, Volvo's 400 series and the Mitsubishi Carisma.
Production is currently running at 200,000 cars annually at NedCar, Hesslefors said. Of this number, 100,000 are Volvo cars and 100,000 are Mitsubishi cars.
"A small investment is needed to take the step to reach 280,000 cars annually. As usual, it is the paint shop's capacity with determines output and this must be expanded," he said.
